judgments.reasoning_cat1: The freezing carve-out turns on whether 'you do your best to maintain heat', a subjective standard with no fixed content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Water Damage Coverage Extension (tear-out costs) and the specified-causes water damage definition, which are consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in with an express resulting-loss carve-back; nothing indeterminate on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly ties back to Paragraph 1 exclusions, which are present.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Weather conditions... only if weather conditions contribute in any way with a cause or event excluded in Paragraph 1' is a convoluted contribution test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends wholly on the B.1 exclusions and their anti-concurrent lead-in; the interlock is intended but intricate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Acts or decisions, including the failure to act or decide, of any person, group, organization or governmental body' is extremely broad and its outer limit is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it could swallow much of the all-risk grant in A. Coverage, though the resulting-loss carve-back in the B.3 lead-in tempers it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statement that the following provisions apply only to specified coverage forms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two of the three forms it addresses (Leasehold Interest, Legal Liability) are not part of this policy, mere surplusage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of six business-income exclusions closes with the catch-all 'Any other consequential loss', whose reach against the enumerated specifics is a classic ejusdem generis question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its utility-failure trigger ('outside of a covered building') differs from B.1.e ('away from the described premises'), and its treatment of suspension or cancellation of a lease bears directly on Rental Value and the Extended Business Income coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short rules for a Leasehold Interest form, including an 'any other consequential loss' catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Leasehold Interest Coverage Form is attached to this policy, so the provision has nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated disapplications and two additional exclusions with specified conditions; internally precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Legal Liability Coverage Form is attached, so this too is inert surplusage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The following limitations apply to all policy forms and endorsements, unless otherwise stated' is broad, with the qualifier undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements do state otherwise, so the qualifier does real work but no contradiction was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six enumerated property-specific limitations with express carve-outs; the roof-or-wall rain rule is a bright line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its Business Income carve-outs mirror the equivalent carve-outs in Limitations C.2 and C.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fragile articles such as statuary, marbles, chinaware and porcelains' is an illustrative list introduced by 'such as', leaving its outer bound open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly excepts Business Income and Extra Expense coverage, consistent with the surrounding limitations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four categories with fixed dollar sub-limits and an express statement that they are part of, not in addition to, the limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Limits Of Insurance provision and expressly inapplicable to Business Income.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes repair of the defect but pays for damaged parts of fire-extinguishing equipment in two stated cases; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the water damage exclusion and extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in stating that Covered Cause of Loss includes the Collapse Additional Coverage as limited below.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Directly answers the collapse exclusion in B.2.k; the two are drafted to fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Abrupt falling down or caving in' with four negative rules is a deliberately tightened definition, though 'abrupt' has been litigated elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the collapse exclusion and the personal-property collapse rule in D.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six enumerated collapse causes with a hidden-decay knowledge qualifier; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reference back to the criteria in 1.a-1.d and to 'specified causes of loss' resolves within the form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of outdoor property with two cumulative conditions; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Property Not Covered and the Outdoor Property extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative conditions plus a marring/scratching carve-out; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Follows the building-collapse rules in D.1-D.3 without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence that the coverage does not increase limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Limits Of Insurance provision in the property form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Coverage conditioned on a specified cause of loss other than fire or lightning and on 'all reasonable means' having been used; the latter is elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the fungus exclusion B.1.h, which expressly preserves this Limited Coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines loss or damage in three enumerated heads including tear-out and post-remediation testing; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with the $15,000 cap in E.3 and the fungus definition in G.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard $15,000 annual aggregate with express anti-stacking across policy periods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with E.2 and E.4 of the same Limited Coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the coverage does not increase the applicable Limit of Insurance and caps combined loss.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with the Limits Of Insurance provision and E.3's separate cap; the interaction of a sub-limit inside a limit is spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment for non-fungus loss is unaffected 'except to the extent that fungus causes an increase in the loss', an apportionment rule that is workable but soft at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with E.3 and E.4 and with the fungus exclusion's carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short neutrality statement regarding the water damage extension and collapse coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly preserves F.2 and the Collapse Additional Coverage, an explicit harmonisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative 30-day rules keyed to whether fungus itself necessitated the suspension; the sampled text has a blank where the day figure should appear in a.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Business Income form's 'suspension', 'operations' and 'period of restoration' definitions, all of which are supplied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named-perils transit extension with a $5,000 cap and a definition of collision; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Property Off-Premises, which excludes property in or on a vehicle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sampled text is badly garbled at the opening, but the tear-out-and-replace rule and no-increase-in-limit statement survive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly preserved by the fungus Limited Coverage and consistent with the water exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition of 'fungus'; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the property form definition and near-identical to CG 21 67's 'fungi'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of specified causes with sub-definitions of sinkhole collapse, falling objects and water damage; closed and detailed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds numerous carve-outs elsewhere in the form and the electronic data and valuable papers extensions consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The endorsement deletes 'the second and third paragraphs' of Civil Authority and substitutes a single sentence, leaving it unclear whether the 72-hour waiting period and the Extra Expense timing rule survive at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with A.5.a of CP 00 30 the substitution removes the trigger for when coverage begins while the endorsement's title promises 'no waiting period', so the two must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean substitution making the period of restoration begin immediately after the loss; the replacement text itself is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly displaces paragraph a. of the Period of Restoration definition, which still prints the 72-hour rule, so the policy contains two beginning dates unless the endorsement is given priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading instruction and pronoun definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to Section G Definitions while the form prints them as Section F, a small internal misdirection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on 'the actual loss of Business Income you sustain due to the necessary suspension of your operations during the period of restoration', and the three Declarations options for Rental Value make the scope of the insured term genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning depends on the definitions of 'suspension', 'operations', 'Rental Value' and 'period of restoration', on the CP 15 56 amendment, and on the blanket Business Income Rental Value limit in the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary expenses you incur... that you would not have incurred' is a familiar counterfactual test with a clear structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tied to the Loss Determination rules for Extra Expense and to the period of restoration; the fit is conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Special Form is attached and its B.4.a Special Exclusions address this form directly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed electronic-data limitation with its own definition; technical but precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Additional Coverage — Interruption Of Computer Operations to which it expressly defers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 72-hour delay, three-week duration and 'whichever is later' Extra Expense rule are mechanically stated but easy to misapply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 15 56 deletes the second and third paragraphs of this very coverage, so the printed timing rules and the endorsement's single substituted sentence must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Covers new buildings and alterations with a shifted start date for the period of restoration; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Period of Restoration definition, which it expressly modifies for delayed operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 30-day tail is keyed to the date property is 'actually repaired, rebuilt or replaced and tenantability is restored' and excludes loss from 'unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the Covered Cause of Loss in the area', a notably slippery qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Extended Period Of Indemnity Optional Coverage replaces the number 30 with a figure shown in the Declarations, but the Declarations here show no such figure; it also interacts with the period of restoration end date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A $2,500 annual cap with detailed cause-of-loss rules; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with the Additional Limitation in A.4 and expressly ends with the period of restoration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: $100,000 per location with a three-event termination rule; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Gated on a coinsurance percentage of 50% or more, which the Declarations satisfy at 100%.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the occurrence limit and lists four coverages that do not increase it; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with the blanket Business Income Rental Value limit in the Declarations and with Extended Business Income, which is listed as non-increasing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layering sentence with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately describes the relationship to the Common Policy and Commercial Property Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Appraisal of 'the amount of Net Income and operating expense or the amount of loss' on either party's written demand; the trigger is stated as unilateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 F replaces 'the Appraisal Loss Condition' with a version requiring both parties to agree voluntarily, and it is not obvious whether that replacement reaches this Business Income appraisal clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard duties, though 'resume all or part of your operations as quickly as possible' is an open-ended obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is reinforced by Loss Determination d., which reduces payment if operations are not resumed as quickly as possible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The measure rests on 'the likely Net Income of the business if no physical loss or damage had occurred' and on an open list of 'other relevant sources of information', a hypothetical standard two parties will quantify differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be applied together with the Rental Value definition, the Coinsurance condition, Extended Business Income and the period of restoration, all of which fix the window and basis of the calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment within 30 days of the sworn proof of loss on agreement or award; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the property form's Loss Payment condition and to the appraisal provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The coinsurance formula depends on Net Income and operating expenses 'that would have been earned or incurred (had no loss occurred)... for the 12 months following the inception', a projection with a long deduction list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the blanket business income limit, the Loss Determination rules and the Agreed Value and Maximum Period optional coverages that suspend it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line gateway phrase, 'if shown as applicable in the Declarations'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations here show none of these optional coverages, so the following provisions are inert.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 120-day/limit 'lesser of' rule; arithmetically clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Not shown as applicable in the Declarations, and it expressly displaces the Coinsurance condition if it were.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limit multiplied by a fraction shown in the Declarations, with a worked example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No fraction is shown in these Declarations, so the coverage does not engage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Activation requirements, suspension and reinstatement of coinsurance are set out step by step.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Not activated in these Declarations; its interaction with the Coinsurance condition is expressly stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single substitution sentence replacing the number 30 with the Declarations figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show no Extended Period Of Indemnity figure, leaving the substitution with nothing to substitute while B.4.a.(4)(b) of the Special Form refers to that optional coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining 'operations' to include 'the tenantability of the described premises' is unusual and its boundary — when premises cease to be tenantable — is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works together with the 'suspension' definition and the Rental Value option, and is what makes the Business Income grant apply to an apartment landlord at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The period ends on 'the date when the property... should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality' — a hypothetical, elastic measure, and the definition also excludes any increased period caused by ordinance or law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph a. is replaced by CP 15 56, the ordinance carve-out pulls against the Increased Cost of Construction Additional Coverage, and the definition governs the Business Income grant, Extended Business Income and Extra Expense alike.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The familiar broad 'pollutants' definition; open at the edges but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the definitions in the property form and CGL, so the instrument is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Rental Value' is defined to include net income that would have been earned as rental income 'as furnished and equipped by you' plus continuing expenses and tenants' charges — a compound formula whose components can be disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the operative measure under the blanket Business Income Rental Value limit and feeds the Loss Determination, Extended Business Income and 'operations' provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Slowdown or cessation of your business activities' and premises 'rendered untenantable' are broad tests whose thresholds are not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with the 'operations' definition and the Business Income grant; partial untenantability across a multi-building blanket schedule is where the strain would show.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition tracks the federal statute with two enumerated criteria; precise by incorporation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel CG 21 72 and CG 21 76 definitions in the liability endorsements.
